name: DHM daily Flood Forecast Bulletin and flash-flood risk outlook
variables: Basin-level flood/flash-flood risk category, expected river stage, 3-day rainfall outlook
cost: free
known_skill_nepal: No published POD/FAR found. 26 Aug 2026 08:00 bulletin flagged high flash-flood risk for Rasuwa corridor before the event (per existing literature note). Part of the dual trigger in the CERF Koshi/West Rapti frameworks (Sep-Oct 2024 activations).
notes: Bulletin archive PDFs exist on district administration sites (e.g. 2021 bulletins), so a hindcast count of 'high risk' days is feasible by manual/OCR extraction. Inputs: ~120 rain and ~85 water-level stations, HEC-HMS (Karnali, Babai, Narayani), MIKE-11 (Koshi), GloFAS.

name: DHM real-time river-level and rainfall stations with warning/danger levels
variables: River stage (warning and danger levels), rainfall accumulations
resolution: Point; ~85 water-level and ~120 rain stations reported in bulletins
cost: free to view; bulk historical data by request (licence not checked)
known_skill_nepal: Height-based thresholds, no rate-of-rise alarm; upstream gauges on the Trishuli/Bhote Koshi were destroyed before crossing thresholds on 26 Aug 2026 (existing literature note). Thresholds reported 2026: Rasuwagadhi 6/7 m, Syabrubesi 5.5 m, Betrawati 4.1/5.0 m, Devghat 7.3 m.
notes: Numeric DHM rainfall warning thresholds were not found online. Danger-level exceedance is the action trigger in CERF frameworks (with GloFAS).

name: DHM WRF / NWP rainfall products
variables: Rainfall, temperature, wind (deterministic WRF; ensemble status unknown)
cost: free to view on DHM site where posted; raw output not public
known_skill_nepal: No peer-reviewed verification for flash floods found in this search. Feeds the daily bulletin.
notes: Needs direct request to DHM for archive and verification statistics.

name: DHM weather radars (Surkhet; Palpa and Udayapur planned)
provider: DHM Nepal; supplier EEC (Defender C350, C-band Doppler)
variables: Reflectivity, Doppler velocity, rain-rate (QPE)
resolution: Typically ~1 km range gates, 5-10 min volume scans (generic C-band, not Nepal-verified)
cost: not applicable (no public feed found)
known_skill_nepal: Weather 2022 paper (Weather radar in Nepal: opportunities and challenges in a mountainous region) discusses beam blockage; no QPE skill for flash floods found. A 2020 paper says the first radar was installed in 2019 in the western region (Surkhet district per supplier release).
notes: Supplier release: two further EEC Defender C350 systems purchased for Palpa and Udayapur (installation status NOT confirmed; release undated). No radar covers the Rasuwa/Langtang north-central corridor, so none of these would have seen the 26 Aug 2026 event; Kathmandu-area coverage not confirmed. Earlier plans named Bhojpur/Udayapur, Palpa/Nawalparasi, Surkhet. Data appear to be obtained via DHM contacts, not a public portal (inference).

name: DHM SMS / cell-broadcast alert dissemination
provider: DHM with Nepal Telecom and Ncell; NDRRMA
variables: Alert text to subscribers / cell broadcast
latency: Minutes; 679,295 SMS sent 09:16 on 26 Aug 2026 after first wave
cost: operator-borne; MoUs required
known_skill_nepal: 26 Aug 2026: alerts reached Malekhu >2 h after first wave (existing literature note); 08:00 bulletin had no standing response protocol.
notes: Included in menu as the delivery layer, not a trigger. Needs NDRRMA/DHM MoU for pre-agreed message templates.

name: South Asia Flash Flood Guidance System (SAsiaFFGS)
provider: WMO / Hydrologic Research Center / NOAA / USAID; IMD regional centre; DHM national user
variables: Flash Flood Risk (daily), Imminent and Persistent Flash Flood Threat, soil moisture, flash-flood guidance (mm)
resolution: Small-catchment (~tens to hundreds km2) basins, ~4 km gridded inputs
lead_time: Imminent threat 0-6 h; risk up to 24 h (sources differ 6 vs 12 h)
cost: free for NMHS with login; DHM staff have access; not open to NGOs by default
known_skill_nepal: No published evaluation over Nepal found. IMD evaluated it for July 2023 Himachal Pradesh event (MAUSAM) and reported it captured spatial/temporal evolution. Nepal used WRF 3/6/24 h products in practice.
notes: Request access via DHM; ask for archive of threat products to compute hit/false-alarm rates. USAID fact sheet: Kamala basin pilot with DHM.

name: ECMWF IFS ENS (open data, real time)
variables: Total precipitation, T2m, winds, MSLP, pressure-level fields (open subset)
cost: free (CC-BY-4.0 subset); higher-resolution via licensed Real-time Dissemination
known_skill_nepal: No Nepal flash-flood verification found. Generic: reliable synoptic monsoon rain at 3-7 d, poor placement of convective cells in steep valleys.
notes: Open archive of real-time data short; long reforecasts (11 members, twice weekly, 20 years) are on ECMWF/MARS or S2S, access conditions to check (not confirmed here). Needed to replace the 5-member GEFS reforecast in the backtest (review 6.4).

name: ECMWF AIFS-ENS (machine-learning ensemble)
variables: Precipitation and standard surface/upper fields
latency: Hours after run time (similar to IFS open data)
cost: free (CC-BY-4.0)
known_skill_nepal: None for Nepal. Operational since 1 Jul 2025; v2 from 12 May 2026 (ECMWF). Archive exists only from Jul 2025, so no 9-season backtest possible.
notes: Short archive; treat as candidate for operations, not for hindcast evidence.

name: ECMWF Extreme Forecast Index (EFI) and Shift of Tails
variables: EFI/SOT for 24 h precipitation, derived from ENS vs model climate
resolution: ~9 km native; open-data availability of EFI itself not confirmed
cost: Charts via ECMWF web (some open); gridded EFI generally licensed (to be confirmed)
known_skill_nepal: No Nepal-specific verification found.
notes: Ranks rainfall anomaly relative to model climate, so avoids absolute bias in the Himalaya. Can be recomputed from the open ENS plus reforecasts if gridded EFI is unavailable.

name: NOAA GEFS v12 (operational and reforecast)
variables: Precipitation, standard fields
resolution: 0.25 deg (operational output); reforecast ~0.25 deg for first days then coarser
lead_time: Up to 16 days operational (31 members: 30 + control); reforecast up to 35 days
cost: free (AWS Open Data / NOMADS)
known_skill_nepal: The EAP's current backtest uses the 5-member reforecast 2000-2019 (once daily; weekly 11-member). No published Nepal skill found.
notes: Reforecast: 5 members daily (00 UTC), 11 members weekly, 2000-2019, no restrictions on use. Member-count mismatch with operational 31 means thresholds from reforecast are not directly transferable.

name: GloFAS river discharge forecasts and reforecasts (CEMS)
variables: River discharge, probability of exceeding 2/5/20-yr return periods
lead_time: Up to 30 days (daily); reforecast 46 d, twice weekly then monthly schedule per v4.2 note, 2003-2022
cost: free (EWDS / GloFAS viewer); registration for API
known_skill_nepal: HDX Centre: only a fraction of 1-in-2-yr exceedances were forecast correctly at 4-7 d; ~70% at Chatara (Koshi), historical forecast never reached threshold at Chisapani (Karnali). Used with DHM bulletin as dual trigger in OCHA/CERF Nepal frameworks (readiness 70% prob. of 2-yr RP at 7 d; action 70% at 3 d or DHM danger level); activations Oct 2022, Sep 2024 (Koshi) and Oct 2024 (west).
notes: Designed for large rivers (upstream area > ~1000 km2 effective); not for steep headwater catchments like Bhote Koshi/Trishuli upper reaches or cryosphere cascades. Check EWDS page for reforecast freeze mentioned in v4.2 note.

name: Google Flood Hub / Flood Forecasting API (virtual gauges)
variables: River discharge/ flood severity at gauges; virtual-gauge forecasts; inundation maps
cost: Flood Hub map free; expanded 'virtual gauge' API for researchers/experts by application (terms not verified)
known_skill_nepal: Nepal coverage NOT confirmed in this search; Nepal likely only in virtual-gauge tier if covered. Global skill: Nearing et al. 2024, Nature (ungauged extreme floods).
notes: Action: check Flood Hub web map for Nepal rivers; apply for API access. India and Bangladesh covered since 2018/2021 (Karnali, Koshi, Narayani flow into India's CWC network upstream).

name: NCMRWF NEPS-G ensemble and IMD regional products
provider: NCMRWF / IMD (India); RIMES as regional intermediary
variables: Rainfall probability, ensemble means, flood advisory products
cost: Charts/data partly on IMD/NCMRWF sites; raw ensemble access by request (not verified)
known_skill_nepal: None for Nepal found. NCMRWF presented an ensemble flood advisory product (2021).
notes: RIMES (Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System) supports Nepal DHM with products; search returned nothing specific, details unverified.

name: GPM IMERG Early / Late / Final
variables: Precipitation rate, 30-min
lead_time: 0 (observation) with Early-run forward propagation of limited use
latency: Early ~4 h; Late ~14 h; Final ~3.5 months
cost: free (Earthdata login)
known_skill_nepal: Not quantified in this search; known to underestimate orographic and short convective rain in the Himalaya.
notes: Useful for event verification and nowcast-style gauge-free monitoring of accumulations; too coarse/late to resolve a small-catchment cloudburst.

name: JAXA GSMaP NOW / near-real-time
variables: Precipitation rate
cost: free (registration for FTP)
known_skill_nepal: None found.
notes: Latency and resolution of GSMaP NOW not confirmed in this search; check JAXA GSMaP site.

name: Sentinel-1 InSAR slope-deformation screening
variables: Line-of-sight displacement time series
lead_time: Weeks to months of precursor, not event timing
cost: free data (Copernicus); processing effort
known_skill_nepal: ICIMOD synthesis: up to 40 cm LoS deformation 7 Jul-24 Aug 2026 at the Gyirong-Rasuwa slope, but timing not predictable; steep north face of Langtang Lirung is poor for InSAR, optical offset tracking (Wang et al. 2026, Landslides) used instead. Chamoli 2021 precursor only found retrospectively.
notes: Screening/watch trigger, not an action trigger; acceleration thresholds unvalidated. Primary ICIMOD report not read directly (secondary news).

name: Glacial lake mapping (Sentinel-2 / Planet) and PDGL screening
variables: Lake area, ice-cored moraine/dam condition, new lakes
cost: S2 free; Planet by licence (research programmes available)
known_skill_nepal: HMAGLOFDB v1.3.0 (CC0) and ICIMOD 2020 PDGL report support screening; no event-level skill.
notes: Feeds rung 1 pre-positioning for corridors with potentially dangerous lakes.

name: Seismic detection of mass movements (NSC Nepal network; global catalogues)
provider: National Seismological Centre (DMG Nepal); USGS/GFZ global networks; Chinese networks near Gyirong (status unknown)
variables: Seismic waveforms; landslide-type long-period signals
lead_time: None as forecast; detection lag minutes if automated, hours-to-days if manual
cost: NSC bulletin public; raw data by request; global IRIS/GFZ data open
known_skill_nepal: Langtang Lirung collapse logged as M4.4 earthquake, re-catalogued as landslide with >1 day delay (ICIMOD). 11 Oct 2026 Budhi Gandaki: seismic record posted by K. Cook shows a landslide near Chumchet about 04:22 local, dam breach ~06:00 (unofficial, via Eos blog); NDRRMA assessment: energy comparable to M3.5.
notes: No operational automated mass-flow alert in Nepal or China (Gyirong) found. Official onset times conflict (04:22 seismic vs 05:30 NDRRMA); a seismic trigger could have given roughly 1-1.5 h of lead for downstream bridges and villages on 11 Oct.

name: Community-based flood EWS (Practical Action / DHM)
provider: Practical Action Nepal with DHM; local DRR committees
variables: Upstream gauge / rain readings relayed by volunteers, sirens, SMS
lead_time: 2-3 h baseline; 7-8 h with probabilistic forecasting on the Karnali (Smith et al. 2017)
cost: programme-funded; local O&M cost
known_skill_nepal: Smith, Brown and Dugar 2017 (NHESS): probabilistic forecasts raised lead time from 2-3 h to 7-8 h on the Karnali (Practical Action summary: additional ~5 h). Budimir et al. 2019 (preprint): communication/dissemination remains the weak link.
notes: Karnali/Babai/Rapti systems are in the Terai-lowland rivers; no equivalent known for Rasuwa/Bhote Koshi corridor.

name: GLOF early warning systems (Tsho Rolpa, Imja)
variables: Lake-level / dam sensors, sirens
cost: capital and O&M (Tsho Rolpa EWS >USD 1 M)
known_skill_nepal: Tsho Rolpa sensor EWS from 2000 collapsed from lack of maintenance; Imja sirens reported in disrepair in an April 2026 news report (local officials, not an official assessment). A GCF proposal (US$36.1M) was reported under negotiation.
notes: Not operational as a trigger; cite as precedent for sustainability risk of hardware detection.
